items.markingKey: (a) A1 A1 (b) f(0) = 1 (A1); gradient 0 (A1); line (M1 A1) (c) A1 (d) R1 R1 [Total 9 marks]

items.stem:
Let y = arctan x, −π/2 < y < π/2.
(a) Given y = arctan x, show that dy/dx = 1/(1 + x²).
(b) Hence find d/dx(arctan(x/4)).
(c) Find the exact gradient of y = arctan(x/4) at x = 4√3.
(d) Explain why the graph of y = arctan x has no stationary points.

(a) Find an expression for dy/dx in terms of x and y.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "derivative of sin x".
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: cos x (x in radians). Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "If y = g(u) and u = f(x), then dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx)"?
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of chain rule.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "Aˣ ln a, for a > 0"?
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of derivative of aˣ.

items.stem: Priya differentiates 4x² − 2xy + y² = 10 term by term and writes 8x − 2 + 2y = 0. Explain the two errors and write the correct derivative equation.
items.markingKey: −2xy is a product: derivative −2y − 2x dy/dx (R1); y² gives 2y dy/dx by the chain rule (R1); correct equation (A1).

items.stem: Explain, without a calculator, why the tangent to y = sin x at x = 2π/3 and the tangent to y = cos x at x = −π/6 are perpendicular or parallel, stating which.
items.markingKey: gradients cos(2π/3) = −1/2 and −sin(−π/6) = 1/2 (A1 A1); product −1/4 (M1); conclusion (R1).

items.stem: Ana differentiates y = sin x / x³ using the quotient rule as (sin x · 3x² − x³ cos x)/x⁶. Explain the error and give the correct derivative.
items.markingKey: The numerator must be v u′ − u v′ = x³ cos x − 3x² sin x; the terms are reversed, giving the wrong sign (R1); correct: (x cos(x) − 3sin(x))/x⁴ (A1 A1).

items.stem: By writing 2ˣ as a power of e, explain why d/dx(2ˣ) = 2ˣ ln 2.
items.markingKey: 2ˣ = e^(x ln 2) (M1); chain rule: ln 2 · e^(x ln 2) (R1) = 2ˣ ln 2 (A1).

items.stem: A student claims: "d/dx(3xy) = 3 dy/dx." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.markingKey: Product rule: 3y + 3x dy/dx. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Omar writes: "d/dx (cos x) = sin x." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: d/dx (cos x) = −sin x: cos x is decreasing on (0, π) where sin x > 0.
items.markingKey: d/dx (cos x) = −sin x: cos x is decreasing on (0, π) where sin x > 0. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Kwame writes: "d/dx (x² eˣ) = 2x eˣ." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Use the product rule: 2x eˣ + x² eˣ = x(x + 2)eˣ.
items.markingKey: Use the product rule: 2x eˣ + x² eˣ = x(x + 2)eˣ. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Omar writes: "d/dx (3ˣ) = x·3ˣ⁻¹." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: The power rule needs a constant power; for aˣ, the derivative is 3ˣ ln 3.
items.markingKey: The power rule needs a constant power; for aˣ, the derivative is 3ˣ ln 3. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: The point (3, 1) lies on the curve 3x² + xy + y² = 31. Find the equation of the normal to the curve at this point.
items.markingKey: Implicit differentiation (M1 A1); substitute (3, 1): dy/dx = −19/5 (A1); equation y = 5x/19 + 4/19 (M1 A1)

items.stem: Find the exact coordinates of the stationary point on the curve y = 4x − ln x, x > 0.
Find the exact gradient of the curve y = e^(2x)/x at the point where x = 2.
items.markingKey: dy/dx = (2x − 1) e^(2x)/x² (M1 A1); substitute x = 2 (M1); 3e^4/4 (A1).

items.stem: Find the exact value of the gradient of y = sec(x) at x = π/4.
items.markingKey: dy/dx = tan(x) sec(x) (M1 A1); exact substitution (M1); √2 (A1).

items.stem: Find dy/dx in terms of x and y for the curve 2x² − 2xy + y² = 10.
items.markingKey: Differentiate implicitly (M1); terms in y carry dy/dx and products use the product rule (A1 A1); rearrange: (2x − y)/(x − y) (A1).

items.stem:
The function f is defined by f(x) = −x + 3e^x for all real x.
(a) Find f′(x).
(b) Find the equation of the tangent to the graph of f at x = ln(3).
(c) Find the exact y-intercept of this tangent.
(d) Show that f″(x) > 0 for all x and interpret this for the tangent you found.
items.answer: (a) 3e^x − 1 (b) y = 8x − 9ln(3) + 9 (c) 9 − 9ln(3) (d) f″(x) = 3e^x > 0; the curve lies above the tangent (concave up)
items.markingKey: (a) A1 A1 (b) f(ln(3)) = 9 − ln(3) (A1); gradient 8 (A1); line (M1 A1) (c) A1 (d) R1 R1 [Total 9 marks]
